gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-traditional-n: Origami draws every letter like a sign-painter's brush held at constant width, with lowercase that feels poured from lead type. Noto Traditional Nushu follows in a plain sans, broad-nibbed and approachable.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-numans: Origami looks like one pressure-free ballpoint line, bold and unfussy. Numans stretches out below it with widely tracked, rope-tight lowercase and an s whose ends hang far from the spine, so the two feel modern and quite different.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-onest: Blunt, brushy and a bit unexpected, Origami sets down its lowercase like poured lead type, every stroke the same width. Onest takes over where the headline stops, with short ascenders above big bowls and a gentle, steady line.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-open-sans: Open Sans is smooth and bulky in the lowercase, with curves that never clog. Open Sans against Origami's hairline-free, single-stroke brush letters gives the pair a sturdy, contemporary weight that never gets fussy.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-orienta: Orienta lets its counters breathe like a hollow reed cut open, and its lowercase sits close to the capitals in height. And across a full paragraph that plain sans stays quiet and level, leaving Origami's blunt marker-tip headline to do the talking.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-oxygen: Oxygen keeps its curves open, with lowercase nearly matching the capitals. Next to Origami's brushy headline, where curves and stems move in lockstep, it feels like a plain sans steadying a louder, more playful neighbor.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-parkinsans: Origami is a single-stroke brush display face. Its job is making a loud, poured-lead statement, while Parkinsans handles the quieter work, with wide-mouthed sans-serif letters that stay crisp even when shrunk.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-pathway-extreme: Origami has no calligraphic thinning at all, just a sign-painter's brush at constant width. And Pathway Extreme, a plain sans, gives it stubby ascenders and a big x-height, so sizing it up a touch keeps those rounded openings clear.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-preahvihear: Origami builds its lowercase like poured lead type, with stroke ends as wide as the middle of each stroke, a bold single-stroke brush look. Preahvihear answers with a lofty x-height and open letter mouths, a plain sans that feels light.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-prompt: Approachable from the first glance, Origami brings a brush-drawn look where even the diagonals match the upright strokes in thickness. Prompt, a sans with oversized small letters and open apertures, simply keeps up.
